name: Anemone

project_scope.admission_note: Both source-pool species learner-approved; county-native status UNRESOLVED for each. Anemone edwardsiana var. edwardsiana is a separate future source-pool identity, not silently merged into this pair.

shared_genus_characters.look_here_first: Find the basal leaves and the leaflike involucral bracts on the flower stalk; count bract tiers and measure each tier's position relative to the full scape before focusing on petaloid sepals.
shared_genus_characters.shared: Spring herbaceous perennials with basal divided leaves, solitary flower with petaloid sepals (not petals), numerous stamens and an achene head.

species_comparison_matrix.look_first: ONE bract tier ABOVE scape midpoint
species_comparison_matrix.basal_leaves: All basal leaves dissimilar to involucral bracts
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Do not confuse illegitimate later homonym A. caroliniana Torr. & A.Gray with A. caroliniana Walter.

species_comparison_matrix.look_first: ONE bract tier BELOW scape midpoint
species_comparison_matrix.basal_leaves: At least one basal leaf similar in division to involucral bracts
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Sepal color and count overlap A. berlandieri.

species_comparison_matrix.taxon: Anemone edwardsiana (comparison; not installed in this batch)
species_comparison_matrix.basal_leaves: Check mature achenes for variety-level determination
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Source pool specifically lists var. edwardsiana; do not create an undifferentiated duplicate card.

decision_sequence: Photograph the full flowering scape including ground-level basal leaves.
Count tiers of involucral bracts: TWO → investigate A. edwardsiana; ONE → continue.
For ONE tier, compare tier position to midpoint: ABOVE favors A. berlandieri; BELOW favors A. caroliniana.
Compare several basal leaves to bracts: all different → A. berlandieri; at least one similar → A. caroliniana.
If scape is broken or bracts hidden, leave identification at Anemone rather than forcing a flower-color ID.
diagnostic_photo_checklist: Priority 1: full uncut scapes for A. berlandieri and A. caroliniana with ruler, soil line, midpoint and bract whorl.
Priority 1: matched basal leaves versus involucral bracts for both species.
Priority 2: flower face and side for both species to label petaloid sepals and free stamens.
Priority 2: ripe achene heads for both species at matched magnification.
Comparison dependency: two bract tiers in A. edwardsiana var. edwardsiana, with voucher-confirmed identity.
overlap_and_cautions: A. caroliniana Walter and A. caroliniana Torr. & A.Gray are different nomenclatural concepts; the latter is a later illegitimate homonym under A. berlandieri.
Both current species are learner-approved but native-range UNRESOLVED by strict project county threshold.
Single provisional photos do not show all diagnostic bract-tier characters.
look_here_first: First photograph the ENTIRE flowering scape (the leafless flower stalk) from ground to blossom. Count the tiers of leaflike involucral bracts below the flower: two tiers suggests the uninstalled A. edwardsiana source-pool concept; one tier leads to the two canonical species. For one tier, compare its height against the scape midpoint and compare the basal leaves with those bracts. Flower color and petaloid sepal count overlap.

genus_diagnostics.look_here_first: At ground level find the basal leaves; trace the flower stalk (scape) to its leaflike bract whorl (involucre). Record bract-tier number and its position relative to the entire scape. Finally inspect petal-like SEPALS, separate STAMENS, and later the ACHENE fruit head.

shared_structure_examples.plain: A mostly leafless flower stalk with a ring or tier of small leaflike structures below the flower.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: whole uncut flowering scape with basal leaves and centimeter ruler
shared_structure_examples.where_to_look: Find the bract whorl on the stalk and compare its position with the halfway point.
shared_structure_examples.why: One bract tier high versus low separates the two canonical species; two tiers route to A. edwardsiana source-pool comparison.

shared_structure_examples.plain: Leaves emerging near ground level rather than directly from the flowering stem.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: basal leaf alongside an involucral bract, both in focus and to scale
shared_structure_examples.where_to_look: Compare the depth and pattern of leaflet division, not just color.
shared_structure_examples.why: A. berlandieri basal leaves differ from the bracts; A. caroliniana has at least one basal leaf similar in division.

shared_structure_examples.plain: The showy 'petals' are actually sepals; numerous separate pollen-bearing stamens surround the flower center.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: front-facing flower macro with center sharp
shared_structure_examples.where_to_look: Identify a single petal-like SEPAL and the ring of anther-tipped STAMENS.
shared_structure_examples.why: Recognizes the genus and teaches buttercup-family anatomy; sepal color/count alone do not reliably separate the species.

shared_structure_examples.plain: A cluster of individual dry one-seeded fruits, sometimes with conspicuous hairs.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: mature fruit head side and macro, with scale
shared_structure_examples.where_to_look: Inspect individual achenes, hairiness and their beaks, not a single fluffy silhouette.
shared_structure_examples.why: Provides reproductive confirmation and a targeted diagnostic follow-up when flowers are gone.

confusable_genera.difference: Both can have showy sepals and achene heads, but local Clematis typically climbs or scrambles with opposite divided leaves and often long feathery styles; these Anemone examples are ground-level spring herbs with a solitary flower on a scape and distinct involucral bracts.
Columbines have true petals with backward-pointing spurs and mature follicles; Anemone has petaloid sepals without spurred true petals and achene clusters.

teaching_order: Capture full flowering scape including soil line and blossom
Count involucral-bract tiers; note one versus two
For one tier, mark scape midpoint and compare bract position
Compare multiple basal leaves with the bract tier
Use mature achene anatomy as confirmation; do not rely on flower color
study_strategy.warning: An incomplete scape cannot establish the midpoint; drought, immature plants and photography angle may obscure tiers. The uninstalled A. edwardsiana var. edwardsiana is a source-pool comparison, not a third canonical card.

comparison_cards.title: Tenpetal versus Carolina anemone: bract position
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Photograph entire unbroken scape and measure from soil-level base to the flower.
comparison_cards.difference: A. berlandieri: one involucral tier ABOVE midpoint. A. caroliniana: one tier BELOW midpoint.
comparison_cards.caution: Do not infer midpoint from a cropped stem or compare different growth stages; bract height alone is not enough when the base is hidden.
photo_roles: bract-tier node close-ups with arrow target after verification

comparison_cards.title: Basal leaves versus involucral bracts
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Lay multiple basal leaves alongside one intact bract whorl.
comparison_cards.difference: A. berlandieri: basal leaves unlike the involucral bracts in division. A. caroliniana: at least one basal leaf similar to the bracts.
comparison_cards.caution: Leaf variation means a single leaf may mislead; compare several leaves and intact whorls.
photo_roles: matched basal leaf/bract comparison with scale

comparison_cards.title: One bract tier versus two: Edwards Plateau thimbleweed
comparison_cards.comparison_taxon: Anemone edwardsiana var. edwardsiana (approved source-pool entry, not canonical)
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Count distinct whorls of leaflike bracts on a complete scape.
comparison_cards.difference: The existing project review identifies TWO bract tiers for A. edwardsiana versus ONE in the two canonical species.
comparison_cards.caution: Variety-level identity and achene traits require Taxonomy + Diagnostic Review; do not silently install or merge the source-pool variety.
photo_roles: whole A. edwardsiana scape showing both bract tiers
mature achene macro for variety-level review
